pr_title: Allow constraining Text in percent of window & container size
pr_body:
# Objective

Fixes https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/issues/1490
Fixes https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/issues/4009

## Solution

With the help of this PR: https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/pull/1493 which seemed like its has been abandoned, I copied the code for the window constraint code and added some code to grab the parents percentage width and adjust the scale_factor for each axis

I've also added a basic example which I can remove if it doesn't offer much value, purely to show the fix working

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/12892064/182011951-20ea1a36-e6b8-499f-9d4a-37dbf1ce2411.png)


---

## Changelog

Text with percentage width now wraps if it overflows the width or parent container

Actually, looking more closely, I think we can fix this up in this PR easily enough.

I think this is the wrong approach, even though it works and it's a definite improvement. It's the same problem as with the pr #6724 that I abandoned.  The text widget shouldn't need to be aware of the size constraints.

I found two bugs in the example:

1. When I resize the window (which itself resizes the `NodeBundle` containing the wrapping text), the text wrap doesn't update properly. (I think to fix this you should look at lines 80 to 95 in `widget/text.rs`)
2. For some reasons, the text that says "It should only fill half the container size" only fills **a quarter** the container size, the one that says "It should fill the whole container" only fills half of it. (no idea why that though)

for 2. by container I mean the item that wraps the text element, the container itself only fills half the window, so the text content should wrap at half of its container, making the text only a quarter of the window size and half of the container.
This should now resize itself when re-scaling the window

I'm really not sure what's causing this, my best guess would be something to do with the `scale_factor`.

The code otherwise looks good to merge though.

Note that the screenshot is the example ran with your last set of changes.
